items.t: 39 houses sold in Cambie, Vancouver at a median of $2,835,000 (middle half $2,439,000 to $3,682,000). A typical house in Cambie, Vancouver spent 8 days on the market and closed at 99.0% of the asking price.

In Cambie, Vancouver, townhomes sold at a median of $1,502,500 across 36 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,200,000 and $1,799,900. The median townhome sat 26 days and sold for 97.6% of list.
Cambie, Vancouver: 85 condos sold at a median of $996,900, with the middle half between $725,000 and $1,250,000. The median condo took 19 days to sell and closed at 97.0% of list.

20 duplexes sold in Cambie, Vancouver at a median of $2,398,500 (middle half $1,943,750 to $2,657,500). A typical duplex in Cambie, Vancouver spent 36 days on the market and closed at 98.6% of the asking price.

How Cambie compares with the rest of Vancouver West

items.t: Of 17 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more house sales, Cambie ranks 11th highest at $2,835,000; the range is $1,549,000 (University) to $4,817,500 (Shaughnessy). S.W. Marine ($2,750,000) sits just below and Dunbar ($2,947,384) sits just above.

Townhomes in Cambie have the 8th highest median of 18 Vancouver West sub-areas, $1,502,500. False Creek is lowest at $850,000 and Coal Harbour highest at $2,255,000. Yaletown ($1,454,500) sits just below and Oakridge ($1,540,000) sits just above.

Of 21 Vancouver West sub-areas with 5 or more condo sales, Cambie ranks 4th highest at $996,900; the range is $613,500 (Marpole) to $1,228,000 (Coal Harbour). Quilchena ($930,000) sits just below and South Granville ($1,064,500) sits just above.
Duplexes in Cambie have the highest median of the 9 Vancouver West sub-areas, $2,398,500, ahead of Dunbar at $2,282,000; the lowest is Marpole at $1,435,000.

blocks.text: By build year, duplexes are the newest homes selling in Cambie, Vancouver (median 2025) and houses the oldest (median 1940), a gap of 85 years.
